beats.t: The otter ran, clutching the pot. Yeoni followed in something closer to a roll. Yeongnyangi brought up the rear, glaring toward the descending crows.
Left! No, not your left—my left!
Use the person running in front as your reference! I have four legs now. This is confusing!
The alley twisted like an anthill. At a dead end, the otter stopped and kicked open a wooden hatch in the ground.
Get in. Watch your head. Oh, your belly'll probably get stuck first.
We just met! No body commentary!
They dropped in one after another. As the hatch closed, wingbeats passed overhead. The sound circled for a long time, then receded.
Below was a cramped kitchen. Ladles and sieves covered the walls. A small clay jar stood in the center. Inside it, one ember flickered as though breathing.
Short introductions. Moka. Otter. Cook.
Yeoni. Human. Pig due to circumstances.
Yeongnyangi.
Cat?
Not just a cat.
Not just a cat, but that tiny? This island really is finished.
Right? That's what I thought at first.
You two really only met today, right?
Instead of replying, Moka set the pot over the ember jar. The same rice-cake skewers. Soy sauce simmered with a hiss.
That smell. That's it. The smell that brought me all the way here.
Do you spend your whole life getting dragged around by smells?
Smells don't lie.
Moka handed over a skewer. Yeoni glanced at the gray stamp on their hoof, wondering if there would be any taste.
One bite. Sweet and salty burst on their tongue, followed by smoky fire. Tears gathered in Yeoni's eyes.
I can taste it. Even with the stamp, I can taste it.
A-are you crying? Over one skewer?
It's not one skewer. It's a whole day's worth of unfairness.
Only after finishing did Yeoni look down at their hoof. One corner of the gray stamp had faded like singed paper.
Yeongnyangi, look. A bit of the stamp's gone.
Real flavor burned it away. Only a little, but still.
That's why I grill in secret every night. So even one person remembers what flavor is.
Jeong Fire. A little flame like a lamp. Even when the sun stops, it remains while someone tends it.
Don't know the fancy words. It's my grandmother's fire.
Moka cupped the ember jar in his paws. Several patches of singed fur marked his palms.
Grandma ran the loudest food cart on this island. Sing her a song, get a free skewer.
Exactly my kind of place.
Bad singers got two. Payment for courage, she said.
Your grandmother was the best. Five stars.
Grandma gets six. You said six was possible earlier.
Grandmother-only exception accepted.
Where is your grandmother now?
Moka's paws paused. Oil spat once.
She passed away before sunset. I've been keeping the fire alive since.
...Sorry. Shouldn't have asked.
You didn't ask. The cat did.
I'm sorry.
It's fine. Anyway, that's why I don't sing. I only cook.
Wasn't that singing earlier?
I told you, a recipe.
First recipe I've heard with such a good beat.
The tips of Moka's ears turned red. He stirred the pot with a ladle for no reason.
It won't come out in front of people. Only in front of the pot.
Why?
Don't know. People's eyes are scarier than pots.
Usually, yes.
Anyway. There's exactly one place left on this island where songs survive. Tonight might be its last.
Where?
An underground stage. Want to come? You'll understand there—what this island used to sound like.
Dangerous.
That's why we have to go. It's the last place with songs, you said.
Talking to you always gets stuck at this point.
The hatch overhead rattled. All three held their breath. Claws scraped slowly across the wood.
Every night. Now I can tell how many there are just by the footsteps.
How many was that?
One. But that one's the heaviest.
The judge has come.
Rumor says that crow used to perform too. Everyone laughed at the very first line, supposedly.
So it got rid of every song? For revenge?
Don't know. Nobody's remembered its name since that day.
The underground stage was inside an abandoned water tank. Lamps hung along the round walls. About thirty people sat knee to knee on the floor.
The musicians beat drums wrapped in cloth. Cotton filled the end of a flute. The singer whispered her song.
She was a woman with cropped silver hair. Her voice was thin as thread, but unbroken.
That's Yeoul. Best singer on the island. She was a regular at Grandma's cart.
You look incredibly proud right now.
No I don't. That's just my face.
But this is a whispering concert.
Sing loudly here and they'll hear above. So everyone sings softly. But they sing to the end.
Together, the whispers sounded strangely loud. Thirty people's breaths rose and fell to the same rhythm. Yeoni's hoof tapped the floor without permission.
They said breathing was allowed.
Yes. Breathing is allowed. They're all singing with their breath now.
The song ended. Instead of clapping, people pressed their palms to one another's. Silent applause.
I like this. These people really love singing.
They do. It's what they live for.
Then one lamp went out. Another. Darkness walked toward them from the stage.
Lovely performance. Now let's settle the account.
The black tiger sat at the stage's edge. Gold-thread cloak, red eyes, red forehead mark. A thick ledger lay open beneath its paw.
Tiger?
We meet again, Yeoni. And the cat in the hat is still beside you. Even changing islands can't separate you.
What are you doing here?
Working. Some of these people borrowed applause. Today is repayment day.
Lending luck and collecting interest, are you?
Business is good. Especially here. Everyone was starving for applause.
The singer onstage went pale. A small tag hung around her neck, just like the one the drumming child had worn in the alley.
Don't touch Yeoul. She borrowed it when she was about to give up singing. She wanted to hear great applause just once.
And she did. Great applause. Enough to bring this stage down that night.
What you receive must be returned. Applause cannot be repaid with applause. You pay with your voice.
The tiger pressed a paw against the ledger. One shining thread unwound from the singer's throat, crossed the air, and was drawn into the book.
Stop!
The singer opened her mouth. Not even a whisper came. People stood, but nobody could approach the stage.
You wanted her song, not to ruin her voice!
How do you know what I wanted?
Then tell me what you want. I'll repay it. Her share too.
Yeoni. Take that back.
The tiger's red eyes settled on Yeoni. The paw turning ledger pages stopped too. For one brief moment, the tiger looked as though it was calculating.
You'd take someone else's debt? Without even knowing the interest?
I don't know about interest. Just give her voice back.
...That habit of stopping when someone is hurt. Still the same.
I won't collect from you yet. Your value will rise far beyond this.
Stop bargaining over people's voices, you striped menace!
Stripes are markings too. Don't address someone else's markings carelessly, otter.
The ceiling boomed. Once, then again. A crack opened in the tank's rusted roof.
The roof tore open. Crows poured down like black rain. At their center, the robed crow slowly descended.
The den of song has been found.
Stamp them all.
They were all whispering! How is this noise!
Whispers are songs too. Applause without clapping is still applause.
The crows stamped down. Thump. Thump. Gray flowers bloomed on the backs of hands. One by one, the earlier rhythm of breathing went out.
People scattered, swallowing their screams. Lamps fell. Moka pushed people toward the back door.
This way! Heads down! Don't speak, just breathe!
Yeoul! Hurry, you too!
The voiceless singer stood frozen onstage, still holding a cotton-covered microphone. Yeoni jumped onto the stage.
Yeoni, above you!
A black net fell from overhead. Yeoni pushed the singer off the stage. The net covered Yeoni alone.
Aagh, it's sticky! What is this!
Let go!
Yeongnyangi leaped, golden claws aimed at the net. Dozens of crow feathers wrapped around his small white body. He was slammed into the floor.
Yeongnyangi!
When Yeoni looked behind the stage, the tiger was already gone. So were the ledger and the shining thread. Only one strand of gold lay on the floor.
Defendant: Flower Pig.
Charges: incitement to song, unauthorized fine dining, excessive exclamations.
What even are excessive exclamations!
The net lifted into the sky. The last thing Yeoni saw was Moka's clenched face through the gap in the back door.
To the courtroom tomorrow morning.
